name: from_raw
declaration: unsafe fn from_raw (ptr : * const T) -> Self
rules: For Rc::<T>::from_raw(ptr) to be safe, ptr must have been previously returned by Rc::<U>::into_raw.
For Rc::<T>::from_raw(ptr) to be safe, if the U in the originating Rc::<U>::into_raw call is sized, U must have the same size and alignment as T.
For Rc::<T>::from_raw(ptr) to be safe, if the U in the originating Rc::<U>::into_raw call is unsized, its data pointer must have the same size and alignment as T.
For Rc::<T>::from_raw(ptr) to be safe, ptr must point to a block of memory allocated by the global allocator.
For Rc::<T>::from_raw(ptr) to be safe, the caller must ensure that a specific value of T is dropped at most once.

For Rc::<T>::from_raw(ptr) to be safe, if U or U's data pointer from the originating Rc::<U>::into_raw call is not T but has the same size and alignment, the reference reinterpretation must satisfy validity requirements for both the original reference type and the reference-to-T type.
